items.prompt:
Read the story below.

Leo fed the ducks at the pond. He threw bread in the water. The ducks swam over fast.

What happened last in this story?

steps: The last sentence says 'The ducks swam over fast.' That is the last event.

items.prompt:
Read the story below.

Zoe woke up. She got dressed. She ate breakfast. Then she went to school.

Retell this story. Use the words first, next, then, and last.
items.answer: First, Zoe woke up. Next, she got dressed. Then she ate breakfast. Last, she went to school.

steps: The events in order: wake up, get dressed, eat breakfast, go to school.

What is the middle event in this story?

steps: The middle event is 'He looked under his bed.' That happens between losing the shoe and finding it.

items.prompt:
Read the story below.

Sam did not want to share his toy. He kept it all to himself. His friend went home early. Sam was bored the rest of the day.

What is the central message of this story?
items.answer: The central message is that not sharing can leave you lonely. Sharing makes playtime better for everyone.

steps: Sam refused to share and his friend left. Sam was bored alone. If he had shared, his friend might have stayed and they could have had fun together. The lesson is about how sharing keeps friendships and fun alive.

items.prompt:
Read the story below.

Aisha saw a little girl crying on the playground. She did not know the girl. She went over and asked what was wrong. The girl said she could not find her class. Aisha walked her to the office.

Retell the story and tell what the central message is.
items.answer: Aisha saw a girl she did not know crying on the playground. She went over and asked what was wrong. The girl was lost, so Aisha took her to the office. The central message is that kindness to a stranger can make a big difference.

steps: Beginning: A girl was crying. Middle: Aisha asked and found out she was lost. End: Aisha helped her. Message: Helping someone you do not know is a powerful act of kindness.

items.prompt:
Read the story below.

Marco rushed to be first in the lunch line. He pushed and cut in front of others. His teacher sent him to the back of the line.

What lesson does Marco learn from this experience?
items.answer: Marco learns that pushing and cutting in line leads to consequences. Being patient and waiting your turn is the right way to behave.

steps: Marco wanted to be first but acted rudely to get there. He ended up at the very back, which is the opposite of what he wanted. The lesson is that acting rudely to get ahead often makes things worse for yourself.

items.prompt:
Read the story below.

Maya was a fast reader. She always finished before the class. She started helping slow readers without being asked. Her teacher noticed and gave her a special job as reading helper.

What does this story teach about using your strengths to help others?
items.answer: The story teaches that when you use your strengths to help others, good things happen for everyone. Maya's skill helped slower readers, and she was recognized and given more responsibility.

steps: Maya had a strength: reading fast. Instead of sitting idle, she used it to help others. This benefited the struggling readers and was noticed by the teacher. The lesson is that our strengths are most valuable when we use them for others, not just ourselves. Helping others also leads to being trusted with more responsibility.

items.prompt:
Read the story below.

Every year, Leo's family planted a garden. The first year, nothing grew. The second year, a few things grew. The third year, the garden was full. Leo's dad said, 'It gets better every year because we learn from what went wrong.'

What is the central message of this story? What role does time play in the lesson?
items.answer: The central message is that growth and improvement take time and learning from mistakes. Time is essential because you cannot rush the process of getting better at something. Each failure teaches a lesson that makes the next attempt stronger.

steps: The garden did not succeed in year one. But the family did not quit. They learned from each year. By year three, the garden was full. Leo's dad's words make the lesson explicit: improvement comes from understanding what went wrong. Time allows for repeated tries and learning. Without patience and time, the full garden would never have happened.
